sections.html:
Enid is in northwestern Oklahoma at the eastern edge of the Great Plains, about 70 miles north of Oklahoma City. It is the seat of Garfield County and covers roughly 74 square miles. U.S. 81, U.S. 412, U.S. 64, U.S. 60 and State Highway 45 cross the city. Older sections carry names you will see in listings and tax bills: Kenwood, Waverley, Weatherly, East Hill, Kinser Heights, Buena Vista, McKinley, Southern Heights and East Park.

The city is large and flat, so one street can mix 1900s homes, mid-century ranches and newer builds. Two houses a few blocks apart can have different school districts, different tax rates and, in the historic districts, different rules about what you may change or tear down.

Vance Air Force Base, a pilot training base, is a large local employer, with more than 2,600 military and civilian personnel and more than 410 pilots trained each year. Student pilots and rotating staff mean some owners leave on a military timetable rather than a listing timetable. Grain storage is the other anchor, and Enid is nicknamed the Wheat Capital of Oklahoma.

sections.h2: Older homes and the historic district
sections.html:
Enid was founded in the Cherokee Outlet land run of 1893, which left a stock of pre-1940 homes close to downtown. The city adopted design guidelines for the Kenwood and Waverley Historic District, and its Historic Preservation Ordinance sets the criteria for applications to demolish historic structures. If your house is inside that district, ask the city's community development office before you promise a buyer a teardown or a major exterior change.

A house with deferred repairs competes against a large supply of older homes, so condition drives the buyer pool.

Enid has hot summers, cold and snowy winters and spring thunderstorms that can produce tornadoes. Heavy rain is part of the record, too: Enid holds Oklahoma's greatest one-day rainfall total from an official gauge, 15.68 inches on October 11, 1973. Roofs, gutters and foundations are where a buyer's inspector will look first.

If you are selling a house with storm damage, keep any insurance claim paperwork and contractor estimates together. A buyer will ask whether a claim was paid and whether the repair was finished. A cash buyer can take the house as it stands, which spares you from fixing a roof you are about to leave.

Seven public districts serve the Enid area: Enid Public Schools, Chisholm, Kremlin-Hillsdale, Pioneer-Pleasant Vale, Waukomis, Drummond and Garber. Which one applies depends on the exact address, not on the mailing city.

That matters for taxes. Millage in Garfield County varies by school district, municipality and technology center district. Rates run from $74.65 per $1,000 of assessed value in the lowest district to $102.02 in Drummond. Enid Public Schools typically has the lowest mill levy of any 6A school district in the state. Assessment ratio is 12.5 percent of fair cash value. Check the district on a buyer's tax bill before you quote a monthly cost.

sections.h2: City code rules that catch sellers off guard
sections.html:
The most common surprises are overgrown lots and structures the city considers dilapidated. In Enid, grass or weeds taller than 12 inches is a violation. The city posts a notice on the property and sends a certified letter, and you have 10 days to fix it before the city can mow and clean the lot and charge the cost to the property.

Dilapidated and unsecured buildings follow a longer path. The owner meets a hearing officer, who sets a deadline that may be 10 days or up to 30 days or more depending on the arrangement. If the work is not done, the city may remove the building or board it up and assess the cost against the property, and it can file a notice of dilapidation and lien under Title 11 of the Oklahoma Statutes.

  • Cut and clear the lot before photos or showings.
  • Secure broken windows and open doors on vacant houses.
  • Call code staff at 580-616-7213 to ask about open cases on the address.
  • Pay or resolve any city charge before closing so it does not become a lien the buyer has to clear.

Garfield County mails tax bills in November. You can pay in halves: half by December 31 and the rest by March 31, and if nothing is paid by December 31 the full amount becomes delinquent on January 1.

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date; unpaid full-year tax becomes delinquent if nothing was paid by December 31
March 15Homestead and senior valuation freeze applications due for the current year
First Monday in AprilProtest period ends when no valuation notice was sent
OctoberTax roll delivered to the Treasurer
December 31First half must be paid
March 31Second half due

The assessor values property as of January 1 at fair cash value. Change of valuation notices go out in the first week of March, and the protest period ends on the first Monday in April or 30 days from the date on a valuation notice. The Garfield County Treasurer (580-237-0246) handles payment and tax roll searches, and the assessor can be reached at 580-237-0220.

At closing, the title company normally checks the treasurer's records and settles any unpaid balance from your proceeds. Look up your parcel before you list so nothing surprises you.

  1. Call the treasurer for a current balance.
  2. Call code staff to ask about open cases.
  3. Confirm the homestead filing, which is due by March 15 each year.
  4. Ask the title company what it will pay from your proceeds.

If a lender is already involved, ask for a payoff figure first. If the house came through an estate, ask the county court clerk whether the file is closed.

An Oklahoma seller must give the buyer either a property disclaimer statement or a property condition disclosure statement. State law says this should happen as soon as practicable and before the buyer's offer is accepted, and a buyer can sue if it is not delivered in time. The statutes are 60 O.S. sections 831 to 839.

If you list the house, disclosures, repairs requested after inspection and agent commissions all shape what you keep. If you sell to a company that buys houses for cash, the sale usually goes by contract between you and the buyer, and the disclosure still applies.

You have three routes: list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a direct cash offer. A traditional listing suits a house that shows well and can wait for a financed buyer. A direct cash sale suits houses with repair needs, probate, tenants, back taxes or a firm move date. Our team can talk through your Enid address and explain what a cash offer would and would not cover, with no obligation to accept it.

faqs.q: Do millage rates differ across Enid and nearby towns?
faqs.a: Yes. Rates differ by school district and municipality within Garfield County, from $74.65 to $102.02 per $1,000 of assessed value depending on where the property sits.

faqs.q: How long do I have to cut weeds after a city notice?
faqs.a: Ten days. Enid treats grass or weeds over 12 inches as a violation, posts a sign and sends a certified letter. After 10 days the city can mow the lot and assess the cost against the property.

faqs.q: Does Vance Air Force Base affect who buys houses in Enid?
faqs.a: It can. The base employs more than 2,600 people, and some of them rent or buy locally for a limited time. Sellers may see more military buyers and more owners who relocate on orders.

faqs.q: What happens if my Enid house is declared dilapidated?
faqs.a: You get a hearing with a hearing officer, who sets a correction deadline. If the work is not done, the city can remove or board up the building and assess the cost against the property, which can create a lien that must be cleared at sale.

faqs.q: What is the Garfield County homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: March 15. Applications can be filed during the year but must be in by March 15 to count for the current tax year. Call the Garfield County Assessor at 580-237-0220 to confirm the forms.
